verses.1: And the LORD said to Moses, “See, I have given you God as an agent for Pharaoh and your brother Aaron. He will be your prophet.”
verses.2: You shall speak all that you are commanded. And Aaron, your brother, shall speak to Pharaoh. Then you shall send out the children of Israel from their land.
verses.3: And I will break Pharaoh’s heart, and I will increase my strength and power in the land of Egypt.
verses.4: And Pharaoh will not listen to you. I will lay my hand on Egypt, and I will bring out my people, the children of Israel, from Egypt through great judgments.
verses.5: And the people of Egypt shall know that I, Jehovah, have raised my hand against them. I will bring out the children of Israel from among them.
verses.6: Moses and Aaron did as Jehovah commanded them. They acted accordingly.
verses.7: And Moses was twenty years old, and Aaron was thirty years old. They spoke to Pharaoh.
verses.8: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Say…”
verses.9: For Pharaoh will say to you, “Give me food.” But you shall say to Aaron, “Take your staff and throw it before Pharaoh. Then he will know that it is a sign from God.”
verses.10: And Moses and Aaron went before Pharaoh, and they did as Yahweh commanded them. Aaron threw the staff before Pharaoh and his servants. And it became a sign among them.
verses.11: And Pharaoh also called the wise men and the magicians. They also performed wonders in Egypt, just as the other gods had done.
verses.12: And one of them threw down their mats. They became dogs. And Aaron’s mat was swallowed up by the other mats.
verses.13: And Pharaoh’s heart became hardened, and he did not listen to what the LORD said.
verses.14: And the LORD said to Moses, “Why should Pharaoh’s heart be hardened, so that he will not send out the people?”
verses.15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning. See, the river has risen, and you will stand before him, with your hand on your mouth. The snake that has turned into a serpent should be taken into your hand.
verses.16: And Jehovah, the God of the Israelites, said to me, “Send my people away and let them worship me in the desert.” But behold, you have not obeyed until now.
verses.17: Thus said Jehovah: “You shall know that I am Jehovah. Behold, I will strike the water with the staff in my hand; and it will turn into blood.”
verses.18: And the bird that lives in the day, and comes out at night; it drinks water from the rivers of Egypt.
verses.19: And the LORD said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Take your staff and strike it on the sides of the cities of Egypt, on their rivers, on their trees, and on their stones.’ Then there will be blood all over the land of Egypt, on its trees, and on its stones.”
verses.20: And Moses and Aaron did as Jehovah commanded them. They made the waters stand on one side, so that they would be visible to Pharaoh and his servants. All the waters became blood.
verses.21: And the river died in the summer. Then the sun came out, but the people of Egypt couldn’t drink from that water. So blood covered every part of Egypt.
verses.22: And the Egyptians did as they were told. Pharaoh’s heart became strong, and he did not listen to them, as Jehovah had commanded.
verses.23: And Pharaoh went into his house. But his heart did not rejoice even then.
verses.24: And all the people of Egypt dug wells around the river, so that they could drink water, since they couldn’t drink from the waters of the river.
verses.25: And it took seven days after the Lord’s punishment to fill the pit with water.
verses.26: And the LORD said to Moses, “Go and speak to Pharaoh. Say to him, ‘As the LORD has said, I will send my people away and they will serve me.’”
verses.27: And if you refuse to send them, then I will destroy all your borders with arrows.
verses.28: And the locusts will crawl out of their holes, and they will come into your house, into your courtyard, onto your bed, into your servants’ houses, among your people, in your flocks, and in all your possessions.
verses.29: And in your land, and among all your servants, the prophets will rise up.
